findings.description: Cast and set specimens have no title/nameplate band at all — only a rosette/moon medallion at the art/panel seam. The creature card DOES carry an angled glyph banner strip, so the nameplate subsystem is inconsistent across the family. This is a structural hierarchy gap, independent of the declared pseudo-text divergence.
A horizontal ornamental band along the very top of the frame is cropped mid-motif, reading as overflow from a larger scene rather than a composed showcase edge.

The card back's plum+gold language is nearly identical to the set-verse family frame (same plum, same gold linework, same moon motif). At glance distance a face-down card and a set-verse face risk being conflated — a face/back separability concern for a TCG.
Corner flourish ornaments differ left vs right, and the gold bezel width wobbles slightly along the vertical rails; visible only at 2x, characteristic painterly unevenness.

Glyph rows show baseline wobble and a few smudged/blurred glyph clusters at 2x (row 2, right end); the leading sigils (diamond/eye/dark-diamond) are a nice hierarchy device but their weights are uneven.
Sword hilt of the ATK heart clips over the outer bezel, and the heart bezel gold is a warmer hue than the frame gold; charming but not disciplined.

Phantom Wall illustration is generic and underworked: a flat wall with scattered dots, and a translucent circle overlapping the crenellations that reads as an unintended lens/moon artifact rather than composed art.

The environment is a flat vertical-striped chartreuse gradient — wallpaper, not a tabletop. Cards cast soft shadows onto an abstract plane, undermining the manufactured-object-on-a-surface premise the staging implies.

A dark backing layer protrudes as a visible step above the top edge behind the rail (top-right, repeated on the cast frame). Because it half-emerges only at one corner it reads as a misregistered layer at 2x rather than a deliberate offset-spine motif.

Back composition is sparse: incomplete/asymmetric corner brackets and floating comma-like swashes that are not anchored to the emblem geometry; feels like a wireframe of a back rather than a finished one.

Sunburst ray texture runs directly beneath body text, adding low-level luminance noise behind letterforms; contrast still passes but the panel would be cleaner with the rays masked out of the text measure.
Stat chips are mismatched in visual weight (amber hexagon vs larger maroon circle), and the slashed-zero mono numerals clash with the book-serif voice of the rest of the card.
Title plate border treatment drifts across families — the set-verse plate carries a dark green-tinted outer stroke the other plates lack.

A: Convincing manufactured materials: carved/gilded frames with coherent bevel lighting, stone kerf texture, and parchment grain that survive 2x inspection
Art, frame, and ground share one warm light temperature; contact shadows sit tight and directional, so the cards genuinely rest on the grass
Panel micro-typography as craft: sigil-led line hierarchy, hairline dividers, and rhythmically even glyph rows give the rules panel real print-object credibility
B: Exemplary information hierarchy: cost coin, type banner (TWILIGHT WOLF / CAST VERSE / SET VERSE), title plate, sigil, rules, flavor, stats — every zone is instantly parseable
Disciplined family color system (amber/teal/plum rails plus navy back) that matches the metric report's sampled medians exactly, with strong cast/set separation
Chassis consistency: identical geometry, plate construction, and sigil placement across all three faces plus the back reads as one printed product line

notes: Two philosophies: A is a painterly physical-object render with superb material believability, lighting, and ground integration but structural gaps (no nameplate on two of three faces, back/set-family conflation risk, painterly wobble at 2x). B is a clean flat-vector system with the best readability and system discipline in the packet but thin material language, a wallpaper ground, and one visibly underworked illustration (set-verse). Metric report: all 11 rows pass; the sampled palette medians and footer-contrast rows correspond plausibly to what is visible on side B's plates and rails, while side A's brighter gold/teal would not land those exact medians — I make no authorship claim, only that the report's numbers are consistent with one side's visuals. One plausibility flag: three of four palette deltaE00 values are exactly 0.0, which is suspiciously perfect for sampled medians vs targets and reads as authored-value-compared-to-itself; not a failed row, so no 8.9 cap is triggered, but the measurement independence should be audited. Shadow rows (+43..46 x, +72..81 y, 58-61 deg) are consistent with the down-right shadows visible in both renders. Wow: A = 8.2 (immediate premium impact, held back by the missing nameplate subsystem); B = 6.8 (polished and legible, but flat materials, abstract ground, and the set-verse art are multiple visible gaps).
